$comment-purpose: Flow's own self-configuration. Flow is a Claude Code plugin: mostly markdown + stdlib Python, with NO launchable app — hence platform=library, which makes /flow:verify-build self-skip (there is no runnable target to drive).
$comment-uiSurface: TRUE, deliberately. Flow has no app, but it DOES author and ship browser UI: the click-to-comment annotation overlay, the verify-build HTML report renderer, and the visual-history skeleton. Those render in a consumer's browser and a human interacts with them, so they are a UI surface and /flow:accessibility-review must audit them. This was `false` until v1.23.0, which meant flow's own most interactive artifact was the one file its a11y gate never looked at — a dogfooding blind spot, not a property of the code.
$comment-uiFilePatterns: Scoped to the files that actually emit browser UI, NOT a bare extension match — most of this repo is prose and stdlib Python, and a repo-wide pattern would make every docs PR read as a UI change. Single extended-regex string (consumed via jq -r then grep -E), never an array.
$comment-visualHistoryPath: Default is core-docs/visual-history.html, but CLAUDE.md reserves core-docs/ for the consumer template scaffolding — flow tracks itself in dev-docs/. Set explicitly so a visually-significant ship can't create a core-docs/ directory in this repo and cross the three-surface boundary.
